name: Winter savory

schedule.notes: Slow to germinate. Easier from cuttings or division from an established plant.
Snip stem tips; cut hard after flowering to keep tight.

harvest.cues: Stems 4 to 6 in, leaves dark green, leathery. Strongest flavor just before flowering.
harvest.storageNotes: Dries excellently. Stronger flavor than summer savory; use sparingly.

varieties.name: Common Winter Savory
varieties.notes: Pungent, almost thyme-like, with savory's distinct pepper-bite. Stays evergreen in zone 7+.

notes: Hardier and stronger-flavored than summer savory. Wants lean, gravelly, alkaline soil — kills in heavy clay or with overwatering. Trim hard each spring to prevent woody growth.
